reviewerAJustifications.justification: The cited index.mjs:4-5 declares exported inspectRequest and shows its body.
The cited parse-request.mjs:1-15 defines parseRequest, but does not show inspectRequest invoking it first; the entry call site is not linked to this fact.
The citations show the function bodies and default, but omit index.mjs:1-2 and route-request.mjs:1, which connect the called symbols to the claimed modules and active resolver.

The route and default values appear in the cited ranges, but route-request.mjs:3-11 does not establish which same-named resolvePolicy implementation is imported; the active import at line 1 is outside the cited range.
The cited ranges support the two named direct calls, but do not establish that these are every call site within the complete allowlist.
The cited legacy file shows a same-named export, but does not establish that it is outside the active call path.
resolve-policy.mjs:3-9 shows the safe-integer and inclusive lower-bound checks, replacement versus default fallback, and returned maxTerms value.
The cited parse-request and route-request ranges show parsing and routing in distinct source modules.
The cited parse-request.mjs range shows the request record, query, and mode being read and transformed.
The cited parse-request.mjs range shows mode trimmed, lowercased, and mapped to strict or standard.
The cited policy and legacy files show distinct resolvePolicy implementations in separate modules.
The cited inspect-batch.mjs:1-5 imports and calls inspectRequest from the public entry, with no direct policy-resolver import or call in that module.

caseComments.overall: Evidence-only review of the trace case. The entry and override citations directly support their facts. The first-call, execution-path, decision, direct-call-site completeness, and lookalike path claims are not fully established by their fact-linked ranges; ranges from other facts were not used to fill those gaps.
